children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were lower Friday morning but were still above their major averages.

Crude oil lost more than US$1 per barrel as there were no new attacks between the U.S. and Iran overnight. Chicago soyoil lost one U.S. cent per pound, while Malaysian palm oil was higher and European rapeseed was mixed.

The Canadian Grain Commission reported 58,300 tonnes of canola were exported during the week ended Aug. 30, down from 118,100 the previous week. So far this marketing year, 584,800 tonnes were shipped, compared with 482,300 tonnes a year ago.

Also that week, domestic disappearance for canola was 294,600 tonnes, compared to 267,300 the previous week. So far, 1.068 million tonnes of canola were used domestically this marketing year, above the 893,000 tonnes used last year.

Northern and central Alberta will see rain and some thunderstorms with the entire province having daytime temperatures in the high-teen to low-20 degrees Celsius. Rain will fall in northern Saskatchewan, while the rest of the province will see sunny skies and temperatures in the mid- to high-20s. Temperatures will be in the mid-20s in Manitoba with rain in Winnipeg.

The Canadian dollar was down one-third of a U.S. cent compared with Thursday's close. Statistics Canada reported Friday that the country lost 42,000 jobs in August with the unemployment rate holding at 6.4%.
